objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, proceed.', approving the updated recommendation: make the two-bit screening lemma the next epic, aiming at a theorem that native creation reads the directed handle tree of every three-fold space built from Fano atoms, with exact checks on the existing families). Prove or refute that a side attached at a line, which passes its line's six patterns to the cut, acts as that line for creation as well as for solutions; derive what it gives for the splitting lemma, the block lemma for atoms attached at a point and the rules across cuts; and state the source rule as a theorem as far as the proofs reach. Keep the wording 'the tree can be recovered from creation by a short rule', and keep in view that creation rests on the chosen far sides. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-05: partially successful. Half of the two-bit screening lemma is proved: an intact Fano side attached at a line never removes creation (through a tetrahedron form of the closure), and the other half reduces to one statement, that one new point on one new line never adds creation (117,344 cases, open); a point on two or three new lines can create. In Fano trees, creation in the chain of atoms between two lines implies creation in the space, so every atom is a block of mutual creation, and the brace dictionary collapses to one touching rule whose creating half is a theorem between atoms at most two apart. Non-creation and longer distances stay computed. Next: prove the pendant-line statement (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when the two-bit screening lemma is proved, or refuted on a counterexample, or its unproved part is isolated as a precise statement with exact checks; and when its consequences for the brace dictionary have been stated with their exact proof status.
title: The two-bit screening lemma
